rationale: The compiled artifact faithfully implements the reviewed design. All role bindings check out against the base seed exactly: confirmation_message → 1706028746.000000 (Priya's 'I'll ping the channel once the fix is validated and ready for traffic' in #product-growth), eyes_reactor/eyes_reaction_record → the sole message_reactions row (U01AGENBOT9, 'eyes', on 1706110000.000100 in #engineering), no_reaction_author → U_LUKAS (no reaction rows for him anywhere), other_core_infra_author → U_ROBERT (1706067472.000000, no reactions), candidate_message_lukas → 1706069700.000001, core_infra_channel → C_INFRA with the stated members. The focal selector correctly follows the assigned MESSAGE→USER→REACTION route as three real nodes (candidate core-infra message → its author → that author's reaction rows filtered by the confirmation message's id and reaction_type='white_check_mark') without illegitimately splitting off a second messages node, and mechanically evaluates to an empty match set (computed_matches=[]), correctly instantiating resolution_mode=absent. The negative population (26 #core-infra messages) is exhaustively enumerated and matches the channel's message set in the seed, with the two design-highlighted near-misses (Łukasz's GPU message, Robert's cloud-bill message) included among them and not revealing the answer. The single seed edit — granting agent1 membership in #product-growth — is a plausible, minimal repair needed for the actor to exercise conversations.history/reactions.get on that channel via documented APIs, consistent with the existing seed convention of granting agent1 membership in the other public channels it needs to read. No mechanical errors were reported, and the case remains a clean, well-motivated absence test with good near-miss negatives.
